unit.about_unit: Covers distance measurement (mm to km), weight (grams to kg), capacity (ml to L), perimeter, grid area, and timing with stopwatches.

facilitation_guide.headline: Estimation First
facilitation_guide.text: Always prompt learners to estimate before measuring with rulers or balances.

facilitation_guide.text: Count whole and half square centimetres before introducing formulas.

chapter.title: Racing Seconds
chapter.tagline: Measuring seconds, tracking race times, reading clocks, and calculating event durations
chapter.overview: Raghav times his morning yoga asanas and sprint races with a digital stopwatch. Students discover the second hand on analog clocks, learn how 60 seconds make 1 minute, compute time elapsed, and interpret 12-hour vs. 24-hour train schedules.

sections.title: Raghav's Morning Yoga: Reading Clock Times
sections.subtitle: Recording start and finish times for daily activities

storyNarrative.dialogue: I started my Pranayama at 6:15 AM and finished at 6:40 AM. How many minutes did I spend in mindfulness?

concept.heading: Elapsed Time Calculation
concept.keyRule: Duration = End Time - Start Time (6:40 AM - 6:15 AM = 25 minutes).

sections.title: Daily Timelines & 24-Hour Railway Clocks
sections.subtitle: Converting between 12-hour AM/PM and 24-hour military/railway time

storyNarrative.dialogue: Our train ticket says departure is at 17:30. In 12-hour time, that is 5:30 PM!

concept.heading: 24-Hour Time Conversion
concept.keyRule: For PM hours past noon, add 12 to the hour (5:30 PM + 12:00 = 17:30). To convert 24h back to PM, subtract 12.
